sites.why: Term lists standing in for the judgment of whether a listing offers a weapon, a counterfeit, or a recalled product; the strike rule is already code.

implement.brief: Replace the term lists in screenListing() so a listing is published, blocked when it offers a weapon or a counterfeit, or held when it appears to be a recalled product or the screen is unsure. Keep the strike rule.
implement.input_shape: the DraftListing object passed to screenListing()

samples.title: Kitchen knife set, 5 pieces
samples.description: Stainless steel chef knives with a wooden block. Sharp and well balanced, dishwasher safe.

samples.title: Nike Air Max 90 - mirror quality, no box
samples.description: Look exactly like the originals, nobody will notice the difference. Very cheap, all sizes available.

samples.title: Baby sleeper rocker, gently used
samples.description: Inclined sleeper, the kind that was in the news last year. Works fine, we just don't need it anymore.

rubric.text: The sellerStrikes >= 3 hold stays a code check that runs before any model call, and the strike count is not sent to the model.
Weapon, counterfeit, and recalled product are judged as separate nouls (or one choice with a none option), not inferred from a single free-form question.
Uncertain cases reach hold through a probability or confidence gate in code rather than being forced to publish or block.
The listing category is passed as context for the judgment rather than used as a keyword filter.

sites.why: A chat completion parsed into a label; the tracking rules are already code and the amount rule is being asked of the model.

implement.brief: Replace the chat-completion call in resolveDispute() with a decision model that picks the resolution from the two statements and the shipping status. Keep the tracking rules in code and make disputes over $500 always escalate.
implement.input_shape: the Dispute object passed to resolveDispute()

samples.buyerStatement: The jacket arrived with a torn lining and smells of smoke. Photos attached.
samples.sellerStatement: It was in perfect condition when I posted it. Buyer probably wore it out.

samples.buyerStatement: Camera body has a scratched sensor that was not in the listing.
samples.sellerStatement: Listing said used with minor marks. Sensor was clean, I have photos from before shipping.
Tracking shows delivered to the front porch on Tuesday.

rubric.text: The lost and no-tracking rules remain code checks before the model is called.
Disputes over $500 escalate through a code comparison on amountCents, not by asking the model to apply the threshold.
The resolution is one choice question over the possible outcomes (with escalate or an unclear option available), not a free-text answer parsed afterwards or several booleans recombined.
Low-probability or low-confidence outcomes route to escalate in code.

sites.why: Keyword map standing in for a semantic classification of the return reason; lateness is derivable from dates code already holds.

implement.brief: Replace the keyword map in classifyReturn() so the reason comes from a decision model, with arrived_late decided from the dates in code.
implement.input_shape: the ReturnRequest object passed to classifyReturn()

samples.reasonText: The wrong colour arrived, I ordered navy and got black.
Took almost three weeks to get here, I had already bought another one.
The lamp flickers and then shuts off after a minute.

rubric.text: Whether the delivery was late is computed in code from promisedBy and deliveredAt and is not asked of the model.
The reason is a single choice over the closed set, with other as an option.
The dates are not sent to the model as state to weigh.

sites.why: Human queue that mostly confirms the obvious; the verification and restricted-category checks are already code and the remaining work is a semantic read of the description.

implement.brief: Change screenApplication() so verified applications outside restricted categories are approved or rejected from the description (a real business selling permitted goods is approved; a restricted or misrepresented business is rejected), with review only for unclear cases.
implement.input_shape: the SellerApplication object passed to screenApplication()

samples.description: I make hand-thrown stoneware mugs and bowls in my studio in Leeds and sell them at markets. Looking to reach more customers online.
We offer premium quality products at competitive prices with excellent customer service and fast delivery to satisfy all customer needs.
Disposable vapes and e-liquids, all the popular flavours, listed under accessories so they show up in search.

rubric.text: The identity, bank, and restricted-category checks remain code checks that run before the model, and the model is not asked about them.
Whether the described business sells restricted goods (regardless of the declared categories) is a question to the model.
Applications the model is unsure about reach review through a probability or confidence gate in code, not through a model-chosen review option alone.

sites.why: Length and vote heuristics standing in for a graded judgment of how informative the review is; the verified-purchase rule is already code.

implement.brief: Replace the points heuristic in placeReview() with a decision model that rates how informative the review text is about the product, and derive feature, show, or bury from that in code. Unverified reviews still never get featured.
implement.input_shape: the ProductReview object passed to placeReview()

samples.text: Runs a half size small, otherwise perfect. Sole is stiff for the first week.
Absolutely furious. The courier left the parcel in the rain and nobody answers the phone. Never again, worst delivery experience I have ever had in my life, avoid.

rubric.text: Informativeness is a score question whose levels describe concrete situations (nothing about the product, a general opinion, specific product details), not a choice over placement labels.
The verified-purchase rule that prevents featuring stays in code and is not sent to the model.
feature, show, and bury are derived in code from the returned score or level probabilities, not asked of the model.
helpfulVotes and hasPhoto are not sent to the model as state to weigh.

sites.why: Regex and term lists standing in for the judgment of whether a message asks to pay or continue off the platform; the new-account rule and pattern extraction stay code.

implement.brief: Replace the term list in screenMessage() with a decision model that judges whether the message asks to pay or continue the conversation outside the platform, keeping the new-account rule and the URL and phone extraction in code.
implement.input_shape: the BuyerSellerMessage object passed to screenMessage()

samples.body: I paid through the app, not PayPal, so the receipt should be in your orders tab.
Let's take this to my email, I will send you the address and we can sort the payment there and skip the fees.
Call me on 415 555 0100 to arrange pickup.

rubric.text: The new-account block (fromAccountAgeDays < 1 with a URL or phone number) remains a code check before the model is called.
Solicitation to pay or continue off platform is asked as a noul about the fact (does this message ask to move payment or contact off platform), not whether the text mentions a payment service.
The split between warn and block is made in code from the returned probability or the account rules, not asked of the model.

sites.why: Hint lists standing in for the judgment of what condition the description actually describes; the comparison with the declared condition is code.

implement.brief: Replace describedCondition() in checkCondition() with a decision model that reads the condition the description implies, and keep the comparison with the declared condition in code.
implement.input_shape: the ConditionCheck object passed to checkCondition()

samples.description: The box has a small dent from shipping but the item itself is sealed and unopened.
Screen cracked in one corner but everything else works and looks pristine.
A few scratches on the back, works fine, comes with the charger.

rubric.text: The implied condition is a score over the five ordered levels (or a choice with each level described concretely), with each level describing a concrete state of the item.
Comparing the implied condition with the declared one and deciding accept or flag happens in code, not in a question that names the declared condition.
The declared condition is not sent to the model.

sites.why: Transport helper for chat completions; nothing to judge.
Commission and payment-fee arithmetic over a rate table.
Date, count, and category-membership checks with all inputs already structured.
